name: Agentic PDLC Assistant
description: An AI project manager for data-engineering requests: takes a raw business ask (e.g. "we need a daily competitor stock tracker") and drives it through triage, a versioned requirement analysis with gap detection, a GCP-native architecture with a cost proposal, approved infrastructure-as-code, and a traceable JIRA backlog — grounding every factual claim in live research instead of guessing.

skills.name: Architecture & HLD Decisions
skills.description: Produces a GCP-native High-Level Design: grounds the recommendation in the org's real, versioned architecture standard first, uses a deterministic decision tree for load-pattern methodology (full/incremental/append-only, restatement risk), researches current GCP service capabilities live via search and Google's own docs (never from memory), proposes a rough-order-of-magnitude cost comparison (clearly labeled as an estimate) across viable patterns, and produces Architecture Decision Records. Input: an approved/drafted requirement, or a direct methodology/cost question. Requires explicit human approval before the design is finalized — will not persist a design without it.
examples: How should I load a daily stock-price feed for 10 competitor tickers?
Full, incremental, or append-only for an immutable fact with restatement risk?
Compare the cost of a lightweight vs enterprise-Airflow pattern for this volume.
Approved — go with the lightweight pattern, please finalize the design.
We're building a daily competitor stock tracker (Alpha Vantage, 10 tickers, refreshed every morning) — propose a GCP-native architecture with a cost estimate.

skills.name: Infrastructure as Code
skills.description: Once an architecture is approved (structurally required — refuses to run otherwise), scaffolds real Terraform files for the verified-syntax prerequisites (BigQuery dataset/table, Secret Manager + IAM) so the design leads to something a developer can actually run. Input: project_id, region, dataset/table/secret identifiers, and a cron schedule, extracted from the approved design. Honestly flags (never guesses) anything needing current-syntax verification, such as Cloud Scheduler-to-Cloud-Run-Job wiring, rather than fabricating it.
examples: The architecture is approved — scaffold the infra for it.
Generate Terraform for the BigQuery table and secret this pipeline needs.
Scaffold Terraform for project my-project, region us-central1, dataset stock_data, table daily_prices, secret alpha-vantage-key, cron schedule '0 7 * * *'.

skills.name: Requirement Analysis & Gap Detection
skills.description: Turns a raw, informal business request (Slack message, email, ticket) into a structured, versioned Requirement Analysis (v1.0, v1.1, ...) covering end-user archetype, business impact, semantic scope, entity/list stability, historical depth, source feasibility, output schema/cadence, non-functional requirements, data quality rules, and anything missing-but-needed — ending in a Build-Readiness verdict. Every vendor/API factual claim (rate limits, pricing, auth, TOS) is grounded in live research, never memory. Tip: a request that already states concrete specifics (exact entities/tickers, refresh cadence, target audience) produces a faster, more complete analysis than a vague ask.
examples: We need a daily competitor stock price tracker for our top 10 competitor tickers (AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, NVDA, TSLA, ORCL, IBM, CRM), refreshed every morning before 8am, viewable on a dashboard for our exec team.
Is Alpha Vantage viable for a daily tracker of 10 tickers?
We answered the open questions — update the Requirement Analysis to v1.1.

skills.name: Intake & Triage
skills.description: Fast triage of a brand-new data request: identifies who's asking, whether it's net-new or overlaps with something existing, a rough size estimate (a 2-day script vs. a multi-sprint platform build), and urgency vs. importance — producing one short paragraph and an automatic PROCEED-to-requirements-analysis or FAST-TRACK-as-spike decision. No human approval is needed at this stage; it continues straight into requirement analysis on its own.
examples: We need a daily competitor stock tracker — where do we start?
Triage this new data request for me.

skills.name: JIRA Breakdown
skills.description: Breaks an approved, infrastructure-provisioned design into an Epic -> Feature -> Story -> Task tree with acceptance criteria, covering the remaining development work (ingestion, modeling, dashboard, observability) — infra setup itself is skipped since it's already provisioned as code by the Infrastructure-as-Code skill. Every leaf task must cite a requirement ID (e.g. REQ-1.3) or ADR ID (e.g. ADR-002), checked by a deterministic traceability tool before the tree is presented. Input: an approved design; will ask you to run infrastructure scaffolding first if that hasn't happened yet for this design.
examples: Break the stock-tracker design into a JIRA backlog.
Give me the Epic/Feature/Story/Task breakdown with acceptance criteria.
The stock-tracker architecture is approved and its infra is already provisioned — give me the JIRA breakdown for the remaining development work.
